solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One’s depressed so one will stay in bed a little longer!

definitions.text: One’s depressed so one will stay in bed a little longer!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone feeling low who cannot face getting up

blocks.clueFragment: so one will stay in bed a little longer
blocks.note: setter's reading: a control on an alarm clock that is pressed down to buy a few more minutes of sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' reads as sad, but it means literally pushed down: the thing depressed is a switch on the alarm clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing this alarm-clock control silences the ringing for several minutes, letting the sleeper doze on before it sounds again.

clue.text: Protested “alien” material man-made

blocks.note: to sit in is to occupy a place in protest, so protesters sat in
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Protesters decry a fabric as 'alien' because it is synthetic rather than natural.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'alien' look like the protesters' word; it is simply ET, following SAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin, often woven partly from cotton or synthetic fibre, so it is a fabric made to mimic a finer one.

clue.text: With small body, old WWI soldier needs trimmed dress fabric

indicators.note: something trimmed has had an end cut off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: ORG is the short form of organisation, a body of people
an ANZAC was a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps; its last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A slight old soldier from the Great War needs his uniform cut down, as if it were a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small body' sounds like a slight physique, but it is an abbreviated organisation. ANZAC loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric of silk or synthetic fibre, used for evening wear and bridal gowns.

clue.text: Awfully lazy soul injecting energy with passion

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a mangled order
an injection puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An idle person suddenly given a shot of energy sets about things with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the eight letters and put E second: the contrast of lazy with passion is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting zealously means acting with fervour and enthusiasm, an adverb matching the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Established old penny not made of precious metal?

blocks.note: base metals are the common ones, as opposed to gold or silver
D was the abbreviation for a penny in Britain's pre-decimal coinage

explanation.surface: A question about a long-established old penny: was it really not made of anything precious?
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read backwards from the clue order: BASE comes first, then the penny. Pre-1971 British money wrote pence as d.
explanation.definitionFit: Something based somewhere is set up or located there, as a firm established in a city is headquartered there.

clue.text: Players frozen here: cricketer turning blue, we hear?

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards
what we hear is a sound, not a spelling, so the word is chosen by pronunciation

blocks.note: a bat is a batsman, the player at the crease
feeling blue is feeling low; the French-style ending is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A cricketer out in freezing conditions goes blue with cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players frozen' suggests a cold cricket team, but it means actors holding still on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a scene in which costumed performers stand motionless and silent, as if in a painting.

clue.text: Scrapping a goal — it’s a pain

indicators.note: scrapping can mean brawling, a tussle in which things get thrown about

blocks.note: letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football grumble: having a goal disallowed is a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapping' looks like cancelling the goal, but it means fighting, which jumbles the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for earache, so it is a particular kind of pain.

clue.text: Remedy we find in our best friend’s coat?

blocks.note: first meaning: an alcoholic drink taken to ease a hangover
second meaning, literal: the fur of a dog, man's best friend

explanation.walkthrough: Dog is 'man's best friend', so its coat is literally the fur of that animal; the idiom for a morning-after drink gives the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a further drink taken to cure a hangover, from the old belief that a bite was cured by the biting animal's fur.

clue.text: Not for good, but as regularly, arriving at island

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: to be anti something is to be against it
G is the standard abbreviation for good
the even letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone arrives on an island, making clear the visit is temporary rather than for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not for good' reads as 'not permanently', but splits: 'not for' is ANTI and 'good' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Say nothing about a Book Club day

indicators.note: about means around, so one thing wraps the rest

blocks.note: 'sh!' is the call for silence
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
a bat is a club used for hitting a ball

explanation.surface: A reading group's meeting day, where members are told to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book Club' reads as one reading group, but splits into two pieces, and 'Say nothing' is the hush that goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest and worship, so it is one particular day.

clue.text: Tough negotiations / where punches exchanged?

blocks.note: first meaning: hard-nosed bargaining
second meaning, cryptic: the Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse, so punches change hands in a horse market

explanation.walkthrough: 'Punches exchanged' suggests a fight, but a Suffolk Punch is a heavy English farm horse, so swapping punches is dealing in horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for shrewd, hard bargaining, borrowed from the notoriously sharp dealing of horse dealers.

clue.text: Single keen on encounter

blocks.note: in cricket a single is one run
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An unattached person eager to meet someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like an unattached person, but it is the cricket score of one run.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance.

clue.text: Vessel, one making gradual progress on way back

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction
in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the earlier-named piece comes second

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
someone who edges forward moves little by little

explanation.surface: A ship inching slowly along on its return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: RD, the abbreviation for road, turns round to DR, and the one who edges forward is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a boat fitted to scoop mud and silt from the bottom of harbours and rivers.

clue.text: Judgement, substantial, was cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short takes off its end

blocks.note: a fat sum is a substantial one
the word minus its final letter

explanation.surface: A weighty legal ruling that was abruptly curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make it read like a report on a ruling; take the adjective, then the verb with its tail cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a recognised authority.

clue.text: Cow’s advance, just losing way by entrance to field?

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so letters drop out

blocks.note: a sub is an advance on wages
taken as written, before its tail is removed
ST, for street, is a way; these are the letters removed
the way into a field is through a gate; the question mark flags this definition by example

explanation.surface: A cow advances towards the gate of her field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is a verb, to intimidate. 'Entrance to field' is not F but a GATE, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow people is to frighten them into submission, which is what subjugating them means.

clue.text: Be greedy, after ordering seconds, but not all at once

indicators.note: ordering things means arranging them, so the letters are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: letters taken as written
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Advice at the dinner table: have second helpings if you must, but not in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering seconds' reads as asking for more food; 'ordering' is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by degrees means doing it gradually, a step at a time.

clue.text: Attack on PC maybe not originally viewed without interest

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, the very start of a word

blocks.note: a hack is an attack on a computer system
only the opening letter
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A computer attack that at first went unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you a PC is only one example of a hacking target.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed phrases are overused and stale, so they have lost any power to hold interest.

clue.text: Marcher is hoping demos are entertaining

definitions.note: the answer is a plural present verb, 'they cherish', matching 'are entertaining' as in entertaining hopes

indicators.note: a demo shows something off, so these words display the answer inside them

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole second, the start of the third

explanation.surface: A protest marcher hopes the demonstrations are fun to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demos' looks like protests to go with the marcher, but it means shows, displaying the letters within the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain a hope or idea is to hold it in mind fondly, which is to cherish it.

clue.text: Arrest and fine upset very old writer

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue the letters are turned upside down

blocks.note: to nab is to catch or arrest
OK means fine
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly writer is arrested and fined.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard abbreviations V and O are flipped at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Retiring perhaps as exam failed first time is a shocker!

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, moving backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.clueFragment: perhaps as exam failed first time
blocks.note: an exam you failed first time is one you sat again; 'perhaps' marks this as an example

explanation.surface: Someone retiring after failing an exam on the first attempt: what a shock!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like leaving work, but it means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock weapon that stuns by delivering a jolt of current, so literally a device that shocks.

clue.text: Daughter fleeing as mouse circles vessel in part of kitchen

indicators.note: someone fleeing leaves, so a letter goes missing
to circle something is to surround it

blocks.note: the simile 'timid as a mouse'
D is the abbreviation for daughter; this is the letter removed
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A daughter runs from a mouse scurrying round a pan in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section, so the domestic scene is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani, the kettledrums, belong to the percussion section, which players jokingly call the kitchen.

clue.text: Small deer to annoy castaway

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
an elk is a large deer
to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: A little deer pestering someone marooned on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small deer' reads as one animal, but small is only S and the deer is large.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk was the Scottish sailor marooned for four years on a Pacific island, the model for Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Where documents kept neat after what’s done initially badly

indicators.note: coming after means placed later, so one piece follows the other
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: a deed is something done
only the opening letter
neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one

explanation.surface: Filing documents neatly after a job first done badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the archaic word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed box is a strong lockable box for storing title deeds and other legal papers.

clue.text: Gas: current, presumably, rising

indicators.note: rising means going up, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: something current is presumably not a former one, a non-ex

explanation.surface: A note that gas, presumably like an electric current, goes upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests electricity; here it means present, the opposite of ex, and 'presumably' admits the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas, the heavy inert element used in bright lamps and flash tubes.

clue.text: School run avoiding centre was better

indicators.note: avoiding the centre means skipping the middle, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
dye that runs bleeds; the middle E of that word is removed

explanation.surface: A school run that took a route round the town centre was an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not 'improved' but one who bets, so 'was better' means placed a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who was a better, one who bets, gambled: wagering money on an outcome.

clue.text: Some lean back to front, getting in danger

indicators.note: moving the back to the front takes the last letter round to the start

blocks.note: risking something is putting it in danger

explanation.surface: A thin person going back to the front line and so into danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' reads as thin people, but it is lean meat; the word is an old British butcher's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Griskin is the lean part of a loin of pork, so it is a cut of lean meat.

clue.text: Top goalkeeping feat — recalled ducking

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the top is number one, written NO I
a goalkeeper's feat is a save

explanation.surface: A spectacular save remembered, the keeper ducking the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' as an adjective seems to praise the save; it is a noun, number one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducking a question or duty is evading it, and evasion is the noun for that dodging.

clue.text: Son experiencing criticism that’s got dad foaming at the mouth?

definitions.text: that’s got dad foaming at the mouth

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
having a bad time is experiencing one
to take stick is to be criticised

explanation.surface: A son being told off has made his father furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foaming at the mouth' suggests rage, but it is literal lather on dad's face; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaving stick is a solid bar of soap that is rubbed on the face to raise lather before a razor is used.
